text: The Patriots' roller-coaster Week 6 victory over the Jets—in which Drake Maye threw three touchdown passes to improve the team to 2-0 in the AFC East—came at a significant cost, as wide receiver Romeo Doubs suffered a shoulder injury on a 42-yard touchdown catch in the first quarter and has now been placed on injured reserve, while A.J. Brown's return from a four-week absence stemming from a right high ankle sprain was decidedly uneven, marked by a career-high three dropped passes. With Chicago awaiting on Thursday Night Football, Mike Vrabel addressed the team at his Tuesday press conference, though the Patriots will be without Doubs as they look to build on their division dominance. The team's 2026 rookie class continues to feature two starters who have made their mark through five weeks, providing some hope even as injuries mount around their young quarterback, and New England will look to maintain their winning ways despite the depleted receiving corps heading to Soldier Field.
